body: High above Earth, thin veils of metallic haze drift through the edge of space. Known as sporadic E layers, these high-altitude “clouds” form from the vaporized dust of burnt-up meteors, earning their name from the unpredictable way they emerge and then dissipate. Now, new results from a NASA sounding rocket — a suborbital research rocket — that flew five detectors through one of these layers simultaneously reveal unexpected complexity in the layer for the first time. Though invisible to the eye, sporadic E layers make their presence known to the radio signals we rely on for long-distance communication. When present, sporadic E can send those signals ping-ponging off in unexpected directions, rendering the technology temporarily unreliable. Scientists have long sought a fuller understanding of these radio-disrupting clouds, but until recently, they had only sampled them one narrow slice at a time. The rocket, called the sporadic E Electrodynamics Demonstration, or SpEED Demon for short, launched from NASA’s Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia on Aug. 24, 2022, and demonstrated the first concurrent, multi-point view inside sporadic E. title: Android Auto may finally have a solution for weather info on smaller screens: Jimothy, the raccoon
summary: No large Android Auto screen? No problem.
body: TL;DR Android Auto is working on a new weather experience for smaller screens, and it involves Jimothy, the viral raccoon. We bring to you a good look at how this new weather display system works, along with some of its accompanying elements. The feature was manually activated in the latest Android Auto beta, and there’s no word on when or if Google will roll it out widely. Google announced a wave of new Android Auto upgrades at I/O this year , including visual improvements and better compatibility with different screen sizes. However, in its current form, Android Auto users with smaller head units miss out on core experiences, such as weather, solely due to screen-size limitations. It now looks like a future version of Android Auto could remedy this. You’re reading an Authority Insights story.
